Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected` in the `FastDateFormat_PrinterTest` class from the `org.apache.commons.lang3.time` package is failing. The bug is related to `FastDateFormat` not respecting the timezone of `Calendar` instances passed to the `format()` method. This issue seems to have been introduced in the work related to [LANG-462](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/LANG-462).

Looking at the test code, it first creates a `Calendar` instance with a specific timezone (`anotherZone`) and sets a date pattern for formatting. The expected value is formatted using `SimpleDateFormat`, which respects the timezone, and the actual value is formatted using `FastDateFormat`, which is expected to respect the timezone as well. However, the assertion fails because `FastDateFormat` does not respect the timezone of the `Calendar` instance.

This behavior indicates a discrepancy in how `FastDateFormat` handles timezones compared to `SimpleDateFormat`. The recent bug reports are not directly related to this issue, so we will focus on the code logic of `FastDateFormat` to identify the root cause of the bug.

1. The `FastDateFormat.getInstance(pattern).format(cal)` call in the test case is where the issue lies.
2. The `FastDateFormat` class is responsible for formatting dates and times efficiently.

Next, we need to investigate the implementation of the `format()` method in `FastDateFormat` to determine why it does not respect the timezone of the `Calendar` instance passed to it.

Let's proceed to examine the relevant code snippet of the `FastDateFormat.format()` method.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
